attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post; not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: The drafter's version keeps Marcus's hedge 'apparently'. It is a claim about the past, but it reports something Marcus heard rather than something he asserts as fact, so it has no firm binary form.

contract.note: The contract is right not to supply the missing pieces: which resources count (only compute or all resources), whether 'AI safety' means only the superalignment work, and what amount was due by May 2024. Any yes-or-no verdict would rest on a reading Marcus didn't give.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own July 2023 announcement of the pledge: 20% of the compute it had secured, spread over four years. It sets no interim schedule, so it neither proves nor disproves that the pledge was unmet by May 2024.
News report available May 18, 2024, before the post, carrying Leike's account that his team struggled to get compute. It explains the concern but gives no percentage delivered and no due date.

reviews.rationale: Marcus qualifies the claim with 'apparently', so it can't be scored. He also never says which resources count or what share was due by May 2024, and the pledge itself runs four years with no interim schedule. Leike's testimony supports the concern but cannot settle it without assumptions Marcus didn't make.
